name: Prefix count of odd numbers + counting array
whenToUse: The standard answer for "count subarrays with exactly k …". The number of odd numbers in a prefix is between 0 and n, so a counting array of length n + 1 does the job of a hash map (and works in C).

card.signals: "continuous subarray" + "exactly k" + "return the number of": count subarrays by a sum. Exactly k (not at most k) is the hint for prefix sums.
card.pattern: a prefix count + a counting array. odd = number of odd values in nums[0..i]. cnt[p] = how many earlier prefixes had p odd numbers. One pass: O(n) time.
card.coreIdea: nums[j..i] has exactly k odd numbers when the prefix before j has odd − k of them. So at each i, cnt[odd − k] is the number of nice subarrays that end at i. Then add the current prefix: cnt[odd] += 1. cnt[0] = 1 stands for the empty prefix, so subarrays that start at index 0 are counted too.
card.variant: prefix count with a counting array (the "subarray sum equals k" form). Each number counts as 1 (odd) or 0 (even). The values of odd are 0..n, so an array of length n + 1 replaces the usual hash map.

invariant: Before step i: cnt[p] = number of prefixes nums[0..j − 1] (j ≤ i, including the empty one) with exactly p odd numbers; nice = nice subarrays that end before i.

legend.text: i: the end of the subarrays counted now
